description: What the row says. split: the track from switch_a to switch_b is two blocks parted at its turnback (the owner's choice, not a rule). track: that track, or the piece of it at `end`, is part of the OS block `block` (the field wiring, or the owner on main and upper). crossover_half: `block` is a crossover half's own OS block.

The lower switch number at one end of the track; on a crossover_half row the crossover's number. Rows are keyed by switch numbers, so a new plan export moves the row with its track. With switch_b it keys a split row.

The higher switch number at the track's other end (switch_a and switch_b in number order, lower first); on a crossover_half row the switch the half's leg A runs to, as its block ID has it. A split may leave it blank for a spur.

On a split or track row, the track's place, 1 to 4 in plan order, among tracks with the same end switches; blank when one track runs between them. On a crossover_half row, the half's letter: 1 is a, 2 is b (HALF_LETTERS), which the desks print (7A, 7B) and the generator names the half by (OS Switch 7a). Each letter once per crossover.
Track rows only: one of switch_a or switch_b, when the row is only the piece of the track at that end (the track is wired in two halves); blank for the whole track.

Track and crossover_half rows: the OS block's device ID (os:15; a crossover half's os:<n>:A-<end>, such as os:35:A-39A; a double crossover corner's os:<n>:<leg>). The reader gives it back as the OS block's generated name (os_block_name), so a rename in devices_field.csv changes no row. A crossover_half row's ID is the row's key. Blank on a split row.
Track rows only: the piece's length in cm, more than 0, for a piece at one end whose track keeps the rest; blank otherwise.
Track rows only: yes keeps the piece inside its OS block with no JMRI or layout block of its own; blank otherwise.
Text for people: why the row is there, with the owner's date.
